name: Conall

attributes.attribute: founded a kingdom in the north

sources: Gardner, Alexander. Popular Tales of the West Highlands. Vol III. London: J. F. Campbell, 1892, 98.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Conall is an old Irish name often anglicised as Connell. The name means wolf. Several distinguished heroes bore it. Conall, son of Eochagh, had sons whom the goddess Grian turned into badgers when they struck her fortress at Knockgraney. He fought her in return. She dusted him with fairy dust and he stumbled and died. Conall Cernach was the Victorious One of the Ulster Cycle. He was son of the bard Amarguin and queen Firm vertebrates. He was a foster brother to hero Contra. He could swallow a full boar. Only he among the warriors quit Da Derga's burned hostel alive. Conall Gulban founded the kingdom of the North in Donegal. His name reached the marketers of Ben Bulben. One tale makes him the victim of a giant in the freeing of Ewin.

okr.objective: The name Conall belongs to several prominent Irish heroes.
key_results: The name Conall means wolf and is also Connell.
Goddess and Grian punished the sons of Conall son of Eochagh.
